'''Nicholas Stephen Manton''' {{post-nominals|size=100%|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 2 October 1952 in the [[City of Westminster]])<ref>[http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/nsm10/NSMbioV2.pdf Autobiographical Memoir], p.7</ref> is a British [[mathematical physicist]]. He is a Professor of Mathematical Physics at the [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge|Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] of the [[University of Cambridge]] and a fellow of [[St John's College, Cambridge|St John's College]].<ref name="FRS" /><ref name="damtp">[http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/n.s.manton/ Professor Nicholas Manton], University of Cambridge, retrieved 2016-03-10.</ref>

==Education==
Manton was educated at [[Dulwich College]] and [[St John's College, Cambridge]], where he read mathematics.<ref>{{Who's Who | title = MANTON, Prof. Nicholas Stephen | id = U26566 | volume = 2026 | edition = online}}</ref> He earned his PhD from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1978, under the supervision of Peter  Goddard. His thesis was entitled ''Magnetic Monopoles and Other Extended Objects in Field Theory''.<ref name="GNP" />

== Research ==
Manton has made contributions to the theory of [[soliton]]-like particles in two and three dimensions. He calculated the forces between static and moving [[Magnetic monopole|monopoles]] and vortices in [[gauge theory|gauge theories]], leading to the geometrical idea of ''[[moduli space]]'' dynamics. This has been applied to the [[classical mechanics|classical]], [[quantum mechanics|quantum]] and [[statistical mechanics]] of solitons. He has also developed the theory of [[skyrmions]] as a soliton model of [[atomic nucleus|atomic nuclei]].

He discovered the unstable ''[[sphaleron]]'' solution in the [[electroweak interaction|electroweak sector]] of the [[Standard Model]] of [[particle physics]]. The [[Higgs field]] is topologically [[Screw_theory#Twist|twisted]] within a sphaleron. The sphaleron defines an energy scale for [[baryon number|baryon]] and [[lepton number]] violation in the early universe — an energy scale within the range of the [[Large Hadron Collider]]. His other work includes the construction of [[type I supergravity]], a 10-dimensional [[supergravity]] theory with [[Yang–Mills theory|Yang–Mills fields]], which is also a low-energy limit of [[superstring theory]].<ref name="FRS" />

== Awards and honours ==
Manton was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1996|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1996]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/nicholas-manton-11882|title=Nicholas Manton|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." {{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220093712/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=February 20, 2016 }}</ref>
